LanguageData.Parametric_SettingDebugDesc: Logs a full body breakdown whenever one of your pawns' Load Support value is first measured or changes, plus a startup report. Leave off during normal play. Dev-mode debug actions are available under "Parametric" regardless of this setting.
LanguageData.LoadSupport_SectionDesc: Carrying capacity derived from the current condition of each pawn's legs, core (spine, pelvis, torso) and arms. A healthy body is exactly x1.00.
LanguageData.LoadSupport_ManipulationCompensation: Superhuman manipulator bonus (scaled by Load Support instead): {0} (limbs {1})
LanguageData.LoadSupport_SettingEnabledDesc: Carrying capacity follows the body: legs, core and arms are measured through RimWorld's own part-efficiency system, and vanilla's Manipulation factor on carrying capacity is corrected so superhuman arms are not counted twice (damaged or weak arms keep vanilla's penalty). Turning this off makes Load Support change nothing.
LanguageData.LoadSupport_SettingExponentDesc: Body regions above 100% efficiency are converted to strength as efficiency^exponent. 1.0 = linear. Below 100% efficiency the conversion is always linear.
LanguageData.LoadSupport_SettingMass: Also apply to inventory and caravan mass capacity
LanguageData.LoadSupport_SettingMassDesc: Scales MassUtility.Capacity (body size x 35 kg), which RimWorld uses for inventory encumbrance, caravans, transport pods and shuttles. This is a separate number from the hauling "carrying capacity" stat.
LanguageData.LoadSupport_SettingNonHumanlike: Also apply to animals, mechanoids and other non-humanlike pawns
LanguageData.LoadSupport_SettingNonHumanlikeDesc: Healthy bodies of any anatomy stay at x1.00; only injuries, missing limbs and replacement parts change the value. Turn off if a modded race or animal behaves strangely.
LanguageData.LoadSupport_SettingInspect: Show Load Support in the pawn inspect pane
LanguageData.LoadSupport_SettingInspectDesc: Adds a "Load support: x1.23" line to the selected pawn's inspect pane. The full breakdown is always visible in the Carrying capacity stat tooltip on the pawn's info card.
LanguageData.Overload_SectionDesc: Lets pawns carry more than their comfortable mass capacity. The further past comfortable they actually are, the slower they move. Each player pawn has an Overload gizmo.
LanguageData.Overload_SettingEnabledDesc: Routine mass capacity above comfortable (per pawn policy), movement slowdown from the mass a pawn actually supports, and spilling of droppable cargo when a pawn can no longer hold it. Turning this off makes Overload change nothing.
LanguageData.Overload_SettingDefaultsDesc: Player pawns without an individual setting use the player default. Non-player pawns always use the non-player policy. Trade caravans and traders are left to vanilla.
LanguageData.Overload_GizmoDesc:
Overload limit

Controls how far normal loading may push this pawn past its comfortable capacity, for both inventory and gear (mass capacity) and hand carrying (carrying capacity). Lower values allow more cargo but permit a stronger movement slowdown.

The slowdown itself reacts to what the pawn actually carries. The worse of the two channels decides. A 25% setting does not set movement to 25%: it allows loading up to the point where the overload factor would reach 25%.

If injuries or other changes lower the pawn's capacity after loading, excess droppable cargo falls. Worn and equipped mass is never dropped, so it can push movement below this setting.

This only sets Parametric's overload factor. Injuries, equipment, terrain and other systems can lower movement further.

Right-click: apply this setting to all colony pawns.
LanguageData.Overload_ApplyToColony: Apply {0} overload limit to all colony pawns
